about: I love the RX3. It’s already a great DJ controller — but apparently that wasn’t enough for me.
So I started making it run my own software.
Because obviously the next logical step for a DJ controller is arcade games.
This project was built purely for fun, curiosity, and the simple joy of making hardware do things it was definitely never designed to do.
This is an independent homebrew project and is not affiliated with Pioneer DJ or AlphaTheta.
controls: Ohhh… you opened the tutorial page.
Look at the thing in front of you.
So congratulations — we already have buttons.
Quite a few of them, actually.
Unless your entire DJ career so far has consisted of PLAY and SYNC.
In that case… welcome to the rest of the controller.
You can still use the RX3 as an actual DJ controller, of course. Nothing about that changes.
But when the launcher is open, some of those controls get a second job:
BROWSE — Turn to select a game, press to launch it
A and B are available for games that use them.
Neon Maze, for example, mainly uses the four direction controls.
To return to the launcher, touch MENU.
And if you ever want your perfectly fine, just slightly less fancy RX3 back?

story: Welcome To Cat Rescue Saga For the XDJ RX3.
The evil deadmau5 - a walking mouse helmet with an ego problem and a dangerously overworked SYNC button - has kidnapped four innocent cats.
Their crime? Walking across his decks and accidentally pulling off the best transition of his career.
Now he’s holding them hostage and forcing them to listen to his sets. Apparently, kidnapping an audience was easier than convincing one to stay.

Fight your way in 4 Arcade games through his minions, and bring all four furry prisoners home. Watch out for cheap tricks, terrible drops, and enemies whose pitch faders are still in factory condition.
But your rescue mission ends with one final showdown: DJ WARS.

Waiting behind the decks is that oversized, drop-recycling rodent himself. Don’t let the giant helmet intimidate you - it’s mostly there to protect the one original thought he’s been saving for his next album.
Can you save all four cats and defeat a mouse whose transitions sound like two tracks filing for divorce?
Save the cats. Humble the mouse.
